text: dune data vegan records cover (1–9 scale) 30 plant species 20 Dutch meadows, along meadow managed wet . clustered heatmap shows species occur together sites alike.  calor_dendro() clusters axes draws trees. calor_split(cols = 3) cuts column tree three groups separates gap; cells stay square slice keeps subtree. trees stay ink colour left tracks; colour groups instead, see k highlight recipe scaled columns. calor_anno() takes data frame whose row names match columns. column becomes one track. Unordered factors get distinct qualitative colours, ordered factors moisture get light--dark sequence. calor_margin(right = "mean") adds bar species’ mean cover. final order available reuse, example order table way:
code: data(dune, dune.env, package = "vegan") sites <- data.frame(management = dune.env$Management, moisture = dune.env$Moisture,                     row.names = rownames(dune)) levels(sites$management) <- c("biological", "hobby", "nature reserve", "standard")  ggcalor(t(dune), cell_size = 4.2) +   calor_dendro(rows = TRUE, cols = TRUE) +   calor_split(cols = 3) +   calor_anno(top = sites, colours = list(     # Quiet, earthy tones keep the eye on the cells.     management = c("#C9C1B1", "#919F89", "#57717C", "#EDBDAE"),     moisture = c("#E4EEF0", "#BDD3CE", "#5F97A4", "#2C3B4D")   )) +   calor_margin(right = "mean", fill = "#708C69") +   # Cream to sage to deep teal, after the "seafarer" palette in ltc.   scale_fill_gradientn(colours = c("#FCF3E3", "#BDD3CE", "#708C69", "#013D5A")) +   labs(title = "Wet meadows grow their own plant community",        subtitle = "Cover of 30 plant species in 20 Dutch dune meadows",        caption = "Data: vegan::dune", fill = "cover") p <- ggcalor(t(dune)) + calor_dendro(rows = TRUE, cols = TRUE) str(calor_order_of(p)) #> List of 2 #>  $ rows: chr [1:30] "Poatriv" "Lolipere" "Poaprat" "Eleopalu" ... #>  $ cols: chr [1:20] "11" "18" "17" "19" ...

code: alt_colours <- c(mutation = "#3B8F5C", amplification = "#E4572E",                  `deep deletion` = "#2E86AB", `mutation + amplification` = "#8E5BA8")  n_altered <- rowSums(!is.na(luad_alterations)) m <- luad_alterations[order(n_altered, decreasing = TRUE)[1:10], ] m <- m[, colSums(!is.na(m)) > 0]  # Narrow, tall cells: many tumours across, few genes down. ggcalor(m, cell_size = c(1.6, 4), cell_gap = 0.2, border = NA, labels = "rows") +   calor_order(rows = "sum", cols = "memo") +   calor_margin(right = "sum", top = "sum", size = 12) +   scale_fill_manual(values = alt_colours, breaks = names(alt_colours), na.value = "#F1EEE8") +   labs(title = "KRAS and BRAF are rarely altered in the same tumour",        subtitle = "RAS/RAF/MEK/JNK pathway alterations in 106 lung adenocarcinomas",        caption = "Data: TCGA via cBioPortal", fill = NULL) +   theme(legend.position = "bottom")

title: Heatmaps as a Grammar of Cells for ggplot2
text: grid can lie flat bend ring. global_temp holds NASA’s global temperature anomaly every month 1880 2025, 12--146 matrix months years. Laid flat, warming reads left right:  Add calor_radial() years run clockwise around ring, months January (outside) December (inside):  calor_labels(every = ) thins long runs names: every third month every twentieth year.
code: anomaly <- scale_fill_distiller(palette = "RdBu", limits = c(-1.5, 1.5), breaks = c(-1, 0, 1),                                 labels = c("−1 °C", "0", "+1 °C"))  ggcalor(global_temp, cell_size = 2.2, border = NA) +   calor_labels(every = c(rows = 3, cols = 20)) +   anomaly +   labs(title = "Every month of the last decade was warmer than any before 1980",        subtitle = "Global temperature anomaly by month, against the 1951–1980 average",        caption = "Data: NASA GISTEMP v4", fill = NULL) ggcalor(global_temp, cell_size = 3.4, border = NA) +   calor_radial(inner.radius = 0.5, gap = 0.35, label_size = 9) +   calor_labels(every = c(rows = 3, cols = 20)) +   anomaly +   labs(title = "A planet running a fever",        subtitle = "Global temperature anomaly by month, 1880–2025",        caption = "Data: NASA GISTEMP v4", fill = "against the 1951–1980 average")
